Article 73

Families in efforts to protect women's rights shall play a role in:

a. providing equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural affairs;
b. preventing violations of women's rights within the household; and
c. protecting women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades the dignity of women.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Buol Regency. 2. Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of Government Affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Buol Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Buol Regency. 5. Women's empowerment is an effort to enable women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 6. Women's protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children who are still in the womb and are not married. 9. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 11. Children's forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so that they can live decently and are able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 23. PUG Focal Point is an OPD apparatus who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that are gender sensitive. 25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 29.

Article 29

1. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 21 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle cases of violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 25

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 21 letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of women victims of violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services:
a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
3. The provision of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by:
a. Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the social sector;
b. Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the sector of women's and children's empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centers or social community organizations that already exist; or
c. religious institutions and/or organizations.

Article 24

1. Health rehabilitation as referred to in Article 21 letter b constitutes efforts that include aspects of:
a. promotive;
b. preventive;
c. curative; and
d. rehabilitative.
2. Health rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out comprehensively, can be accessed 24 (twenty-four) hours at the Regional General Hospital, is of quality and is carried out in accordance with health service standards.
3. Women victims of violence have the right to free health services, including:
a. medical services;
b. medicolegal services; and
c. visum.
4. Further provisions regarding the procedures for implementing health services as referred to in paragraph (3) are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 27

1. The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women victims of violence.
2. The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 25 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. The criteria for women victims of violence who require safe houses include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
5. The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
6. Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated in a Regent Regulation (Peraturan Bupati).

Article 32

1. Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women victims of violence with their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for the victim.
2. Social reintegration is aimed so that:
a. women victims of violence can resume their social life; and
b. women victims of violence can have a decent life.
3. Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 75

1. Guidance on women's empowerment and child protection shall be conducted by the Regional Government.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of:
a. providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on the prevention and handling of violence;
b. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
c. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
d. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
e. improving the professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against women and children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
3. The Regent shall have the authority to conduct guidance in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection.

CHAPTER IV

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Part One

General

Part Two

Prevention of Acts of Violence Against Women

Article 31

1. Return is aimed at returning women victims of violence to their region of origin.
2. Return of women victims of violence is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

Article 71

1. Community participation in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participates in prevention and provides support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provides protection to victims and emergency assistance;
c. provides information from/or reports violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
d. monitors the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
2. Families and Parents are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and children.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Paragraph 3

Social Field

Article 20

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear

Paragraph (2)

Letter a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Letter b Sufficiently clear

Letter c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values, and social status.

Letter d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only by people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.

Letter e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.

Letter f What is meant by respecting individual differences (individual differences) is that each individual must be viewed as unique; each person has a different background, life experience, and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism), so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition is, or whatever information comes from the victim, will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/actions to be taken.

Letter i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational, and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled/difable/disable women have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind, or those experiencing intellectual disabilities. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Letter j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties; however, with proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made to ensure that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to their identity or case narrative.

Letter k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood, and can openly tell their problems.

Letter l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and the full exercise of their rights to survival, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination, and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child (Convention on the Rights of the Child) and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women).

Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Letter i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational, and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled/difable/disable women have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind, or those experiencing intellectual disabilities. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Letter j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties; however, with proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made to ensure that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to their identity or case narrative.

Letter k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood, and can openly tell their problems.

Letter l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and the full exercise of their rights to survival, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination, and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child (Convention on the Rights of the Child) and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women).

CHAPTER IV

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Part One

General

CHAPTER II

RIGHTS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 2

Every woman and child has basic rights as a human being that must be protected, promoted, upheld and fulfilled in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 77

1. The Regent shall conduct supervision and evaluation of the implementation of women and child protection periodically once (1) every 3 (three) months.
2. In conducting supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent may appoint a PD in accordance with its duties and functions.
3. The results of supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall constitute evaluation material for the policy of women and child protection programs in the Region.

Part Two

Prevention of Acts of Violence Against Women

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Buol Regency. 2. Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of Government Affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Buol Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Buol Regency. 5. Women's empowerment is an effort to enable women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 6. Women's protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children who are still in the womb and are not married. 9. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 11. Children's forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so that they can live decently and are able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 23. PUG Focal Point is an OPD apparatus who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that are gender sensitive. 25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 29.

Article 71

1. Community participation in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participates in prevention and provides support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provides protection to victims and emergency assistance;
c. provides information from/or reports violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
d. monitors the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
2. Families and Parents are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and children.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 6

Letter a Sufficiently clear Letter b What is meant by gender justice is a fair condition and treatment of women and men, so that justice for women and men is realized, steps are needed to stop things that politically and socio-culturally can hinder women and men from being able to play a role and enjoy the results of their role.

What is meant by gender equality is the equality of conditions and positions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, educational, defense, national security activities and equality in enjoying development results with balanced impacts.

Letter c What is meant by local wisdom is good cultural values that exist in a society, because every culture teaches certain ways, rules or methods to obtain knowledge or truth about something.

Letter d Sufficiently clear Letter e What is meant by non-discrimination is that every woman and child without exception has the right to receive services related to the violence they experience, no one may be rejected or given priority over others except on the basis of certain emergency considerations.

Letter f Sufficiently clear Letter g Sufficiently clear Letter h Sufficiently clear

Article 73

Families in efforts to protect women's rights shall play a role in:

a. providing equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural affairs;
b. preventing violations of women's rights within the household; and
c. protecting women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades the dignity of women.

3. The Regent appoints the Head of the Regional Apparatus that administers Governmental Affairs in the field of Regional Development Planning as Chair of the gender mainstreaming Working Group and the Head of the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection as Head of the Secretariat of the gender mainstreaming Working Group.

Article 29

1. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 21 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle cases of violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

3. Regional Government, community, family and parents are obligated to ensure that children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Article 71

1. Community participation in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participates in prevention and provides support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provides protection to victims and emergency assistance;
c. provides information from/or reports violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and

2. Families and Parents are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and children.

Article 20

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear

Paragraph (2)

Letter a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Letter b Sufficiently clear

Letter c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values, and social status.

Letter d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only by people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.

Letter e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.

Letter f What is meant by respecting individual differences (individual differences) is that each individual must be viewed as unique; each person has a different background, life experience, and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism), so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition is, or whatever information comes from the victim, will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/actions to be taken.

Letter i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational, and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled/difable/disable women have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind, or those experiencing intellectual disabilities. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Letter j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties; however, with proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made to ensure that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to their identity or case narrative.

Letter k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood, and can openly tell their problems.

Letter l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and the full exercise of their rights to survival, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination, and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child (Convention on the Rights of the Child) and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women).

Letter i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational, and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled/difable/disable women have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind, or those experiencing intellectual disabilities. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Letter j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties; however, with proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made to ensure that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to their identity or case narrative.

Letter k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood, and can openly tell their problems.

Letter l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and the full exercise of their rights to survival, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination, and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child (Convention on the Rights of the Child) and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women).

Article 27

Article 1

Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of Government Affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Women's empowerment is an effort to enable women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 6. Women's protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children who are still in the womb and are not married. 9. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Letter i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational, and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled/difable/disable women have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind, or those experiencing intellectual disabilities. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Letter j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties; however, with proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made to ensure that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to their identity or case narrative.

Letter k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood, and can openly tell their problems.

Letter l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and the full exercise of their rights to survival, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination, and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child (Convention on the Rights of the Child) and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women).

Women's protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so that they can live decently and are able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 23. PUG Focal Point is an OPD apparatus who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 29.

Article 20

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear

Paragraph (2)

Letter a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Letter b Sufficiently clear

Letter c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values, and social status.

Letter d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only by people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.

Letter e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.

Letter f What is meant by respecting individual differences (individual differences) is that each individual must be viewed as unique; each person has a different background, life experience, and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism), so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition is, or whatever information comes from the victim, will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/actions to be taken.

Letter i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational, and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled/difable/disable women have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind, or those experiencing intellectual disabilities. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Letter j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties; however, with proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made to ensure that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to their identity or case narrative.

Letter k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood, and can openly tell their problems.

Letter l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and the full exercise of their rights to survival, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination, and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child (Convention on the Rights of the Child) and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women).

Guidance and counseling is an effort of psychological recovery and systematic efforts regarding differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 30. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 31. Gender sensitivity or gender awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 32. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities. 33. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including human trafficking, which is formed by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, science and technology information centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), shelter homes, children's friend telephone (TESSA) 129 or other forms. 34. Community Organization is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the goals of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila. 35. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 36. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line up or down to the third degree. 37. Customs are local wisdom values that apply and are still applied from generation to generation in the community environment. 38. Child-Friendly Regency Task Force is a coordinating body at the regency level that coordinates policy efforts, programs and activities to realize a child-friendly regency. 39. Regional Action Plan for Child-Friendly Regency Development is a document containing policies, programs and activities to realize a Child-Friendly Regency.

Effectiveness of Services for Women Victims of Violence

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 75

1. Guidance on women's empowerment and child protection shall be conducted by the Regional Government.

d. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and

Article 73

b. preventing violations of women's rights within the household; and
c. protecting women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades the dignity of women.

CHAPTER XI FINANCING

Article 78 (1) The Regional Government is obligated to provide a budget for the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs and activities through the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget and/or other regional financial sources in accordance with the regional financial capacity.

Article 27

1. The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women victims of violence.
2. The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 25 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

4. The criteria for women victims of violence who require safe houses include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or

5. The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
6. Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated in a Regent Regulation (Peraturan Bupati).

Article 31

1. Return is aimed at returning women victims of violence to their region of origin.
2. Return of women victims of violence is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

Article 24

1. Health rehabilitation as referred to in Article 21 letter b constitutes efforts that include aspects of:
a. promotive;
b. preventive;
c. curative; and
d. rehabilitative.
2. Health rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out comprehensively, can be accessed 24 (twenty-four) hours at the Regional General Hospital, is of quality and is carried out in accordance with health service standards.

a. medical services;
b. medicolegal services; and
c. visum.

Article 20

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear

Paragraph (2)

Letter a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Letter b Sufficiently clear

Letter c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values, and social status.

Letter d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only by people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.

Letter e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.

Letter f What is meant by respecting individual differences (individual differences) is that each individual must be viewed as unique; each person has a different background, life experience, and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism), so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition is, or whatever information comes from the victim, will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/actions to be taken.

Letter i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational, and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled/difable/disable women have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind, or those experiencing intellectual disabilities. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Letter j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties; however, with proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made to ensure that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to their identity or case narrative.

Letter k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood, and can openly tell their problems.

Letter l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and the full exercise of their rights to survival, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination, and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child (Convention on the Rights of the Child) and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women).

Article 75

1. Guidance on women's empowerment and child protection shall be conducted by the Regional Government.

a. participates in prevention and provides support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provides protection to victims and emergency assistance;

Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. CHAPTER IV

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Part One

General

Article 71

1. Community participation in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participates in prevention and provides support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provides protection to victims and emergency assistance;
c. provides information from/or reports violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
d. monitors the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
2. Families and Parents are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and children.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 27

1. The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women victims of violence.
2. The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 25 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. The criteria for women victims of violence who require safe houses include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
5. The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
6. Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated in a Regent Regulation (Peraturan Bupati).

Article 73

Families in efforts to protect women's rights shall play a role in:

a. providing equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural affairs;
b. preventing violations of women's rights within the household; and
c. protecting women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades the dignity of women.

Part Two

Prevention of Acts of Violence Against Women

Article 29

1. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 21 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle cases of violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

CHAPTER II

RIGHTS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 2

Every woman and child has basic rights as a human being that must be protected, promoted, upheld and fulfilled in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 24

1. Health rehabilitation as referred to in Article 21 letter b constitutes efforts that include aspects of:
a. promotive;
b. preventive;
c. curative; and
d. rehabilitative.
2. Health rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out comprehensively, can be accessed 24 (twenty-four) hours at the Regional General Hospital, is of quality and is carried out in accordance with health service standards.
3. Women victims of violence have the right to free health services, including:
a. medical services;
b. medicolegal services; and
c. visum.
4. Further provisions regarding the procedures for implementing health services as referred to in paragraph (3) are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 25

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 21 letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of women victims of violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services:
a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
3. The provision of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by:
a. Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the social sector;
b. Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the sector of women's and children's empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centers or social community organizations that already exist; or
c. religious institutions and/or organizations.

Article 32

1. Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women victims of violence with their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for the victim.
2. Social reintegration is aimed so that:
a. women victims of violence can resume their social life; and
b. women victims of violence can have a decent life.
3. Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 75

1. Guidance on women's empowerment and child protection shall be conducted by the Regional Government.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of:
a. providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on the prevention and handling of violence;
b. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
c. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
d. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
e. improving the professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against women and children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
3. The Regent shall have the authority to conduct guidance in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Buol Regency. 2. Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of Government Affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Buol Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Buol Regency. 5. Women's empowerment is an effort to enable women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 6. Women's protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children who are still in the womb and are not married. 9. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 11. Children's forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so that they can live decently and are able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 23. PUG Focal Point is an OPD apparatus who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that are gender sensitive. 25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 29.

Article 20

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear

Paragraph (2)

Letter a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Letter b Sufficiently clear

Letter c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values, and social status.

Letter d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only by people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.

Letter e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.

Letter f What is meant by respecting individual differences (individual differences) is that each individual must be viewed as unique; each person has a different background, life experience, and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism), so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition is, or whatever information comes from the victim, will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/actions to be taken.

Letter i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational, and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled/difable/disable women have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind, or those experiencing intellectual disabilities. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Letter j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties; however, with proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made to ensure that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to their identity or case narrative.

Letter k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood, and can openly tell their problems.

Letter l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and the full exercise of their rights to survival, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination, and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child (Convention on the Rights of the Child) and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women).

Article 34

1. Employers who employ women are obliged to maintain decency, safety and security while at the workplace.

Article 35

1. Female workers/laborers under the age of 18 (eighteen) years are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
2. Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant female workers/laborers who according to a doctor's statement are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy.
3. Employers who employ female workers/laborers between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB, are obliged to:
a. provide nutritious food and drinks; and
b. maintain decency and security while at the workplace.
4. Employers are obliged to provide shuttle transportation for female workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB until 05.00 WIB.

Article 20

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear

Paragraph (2)

Letter a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Letter b Sufficiently clear

Letter c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values, and social status.

Letter d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only by people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.

Letter e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.

Letter f What is meant by respecting individual differences (individual differences) is that each individual must be viewed as unique; each person has a different background, life experience, and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism), so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition is, or whatever information comes from the victim, will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/actions to be taken.

Letter i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational, and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled/difable/disable women have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind, or those experiencing intellectual disabilities. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Letter j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties; however, with proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made to ensure that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to their identity or case narrative.

Letter k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood, and can openly tell their problems.

Letter l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and the full exercise of their rights to survival, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination, and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child (Convention on the Rights of the Child) and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women).

Article 25

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 21 letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of women victims of violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services:
a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
3. The provision of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by:
a. Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the social sector;
b. Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the sector of women's and children's empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centers or social community organizations that already exist; or
c. religious institutions and/or organizations.

Article 77

1. The Regent shall conduct supervision and evaluation of the implementation of women and child protection periodically once (1) every 3 (three) months.
2. In conducting supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent may appoint a PD in accordance with its duties and functions.
3. The results of supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall constitute evaluation material for the policy of women and child protection programs in the Region.

Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 23. PUG Focal Point is an OPD apparatus who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 29.
