Article 20

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear

Paragraph (2)

Letter a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Letter b Sufficiently clear

Letter c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values, and social status.

Letter d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only by people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.

Letter e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.

Letter f What is meant by respecting individual differences (individual differences) is that each individual must be viewed as unique; each person has a different background, life experience, and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism), so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition is, or whatever information comes from the victim, will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/actions to be taken.

Letter i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational, and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled/difable/disable women have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind, or those experiencing intellectual disabilities. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Letter j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties; however, with proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made to ensure that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to their identity or case narrative.

Letter k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood, and can openly tell their problems.

Letter l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and the full exercise of their rights to survival, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination, and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child (Convention on the Rights of the Child) and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women).

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear

Paragraph (2)

Letter a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Letter b Sufficiently clear

Letter c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values, and social status.

Letter d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only by people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.

Letter e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.

Letter f What is meant by respecting individual differences (individual differences) is that each individual must be viewed as unique; each person has a different background, life experience, and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism), so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition is, or whatever information comes from the victim, will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/actions to be taken.

Letter i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational, and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled/difable/disable women have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind, or those experiencing intellectual disabilities. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Letter j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties; however, with proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made to ensure that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to their identity or case narrative.

Letter k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood, and can openly tell their problems.

Letter l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and the full exercise of their rights to survival, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination, and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child (Convention on the Rights of the Child) and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women).

Letter c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values, and social status.

Women's protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children who are still in the womb and are not married. 9. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 11. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so that they can live decently and are able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries. 20. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 29.

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 75

1. Guidance on women's empowerment and child protection shall be conducted by the Regional Government.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of:
a. providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on the prevention and handling of violence;
b. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
c. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
d. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
e. improving the professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against women and children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.

Social Field

Article 20

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear

Paragraph (2)

Letter a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Letter b Sufficiently clear

Letter c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values, and social status.

Letter d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only by people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.

Letter e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.

Letter f What is meant by respecting individual differences (individual differences) is that each individual must be viewed as unique; each person has a different background, life experience, and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism), so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition is, or whatever information comes from the victim, will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/actions to be taken.

Letter i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational, and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled/difable/disable women have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind, or those experiencing intellectual disabilities. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Letter j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties; however, with proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made to ensure that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to their identity or case narrative.

Letter k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood, and can openly tell their problems.

Letter l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and the full exercise of their rights to survival, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination, and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child (Convention on the Rights of the Child) and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women).

Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line up or down to the third degree. 37. Customs are local wisdom values that apply and are still applied from generation to generation in the community environment. 38. Child-Friendly Regency Task Force is a coordinating body at the regency level that coordinates policy efforts, programs and activities to realize a child-friendly regency. 39. Regional Action Plan for Child-Friendly Regency Development is a document containing policies, programs and activities to realize a Child-Friendly Regency.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Buol Regency. 2. Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of Government Affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Buol Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Buol Regency. 5. Women's empowerment is an effort to enable women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 6. Women's protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children who are still in the womb and are not married. 9. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 11. Children's forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so that they can live decently and are able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 23. PUG Focal Point is an OPD apparatus who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that are gender sensitive. 25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 29.

CHAPTER V

IMPROVING FAMILY QUALITY

Article 36

1. In order to improve family quality, the Regional Government is responsible for:
a. making efforts to improve family quality to realize gender equality and children's rights;
b. providing services for families in realizing gender equality and children's rights; and
c. strengthening and developing institutions that provide family quality improvement services.
2. The responsibility of the Regional Government in efforts to improve family quality as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by Regional Apparatus in accordance with their duties and functions.

Paragraph 1

General

Article 25

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 21 letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of women victims of violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services:
a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
3. The provision of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by:
a. Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the social sector;
b. Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the sector of women's and children's empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centers or social community organizations that already exist; or
c. religious institutions and/or organizations.

Article 64

1. In organizing the fulfillment of children's rights to express opinions and participate, Regional Government facilitates the formation of a children's forum.
2. Children's forum as referred to in paragraph (1) is a representation of children in the region, both representation of children's geographical domicile, components of children's socio-cultural groups and children's educational background.
3. In every formulation of policies related to children, Regional Government is obligated to consider and accommodate children's opinions submitted through the children's participation forum.
4. Further provisions regarding the formation of children's forum as referred to in paragraph (1) through paragraph (3) are stipulated by Regent's Decree.

Article 29

1. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 21 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle cases of violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 10

1. In an effort to accelerate the institutionalization of gender mainstreaming, a gender mainstreaming working group is established in all Regional Apparatus.
2. Members of the gender mainstreaming working group are all heads/leaders of Regional Apparatus.
3. The Regent appoints the Head of the Regional Apparatus that administers Governmental Affairs in the field of Regional Development Planning as Chair of the gender mainstreaming Working Group and the Head of the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection as Head of the Secretariat of the gender mainstreaming Working Group.
4. The establishment of the gender mainstreaming working group as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by Regent's Decree.

Article 27

1. The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women victims of violence.
2. The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 25 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. The criteria for women victims of violence who require safe houses include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
5. The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
6. Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated in a Regent Regulation (Peraturan Bupati).

Article 78 (1) The Regional Government is obligated to provide a budget for the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs and activities through the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget and/or other regional financial sources in accordance with the regional financial capacity.

2. Financing for the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs and activities as referred to in paragraph (1) is sourced from: a. the regional revenue and expenditure budget; and b. other lawful sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 53

1. Regional Government is obligated to provide comprehensive health services for children, so that every child obtains optimal health status from the womb.
2. Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;
b. exemption from cost burden for malnourished children, children with disabilities, children with special needs, children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, child victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, children who are victims of violence, and child victims of human trafficking.
3. Regional Government, community, family and parents are obligated to ensure that children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.
